steps.body: Sometimes two objects cannot be moved together. A third object can carry the comparison between them.
steps.narration: Sometimes two objects cannot be moved together. A third object can carry the comparison between them.

widget.prompt: Use this string as the go-between: compare it fairly with the pole.
widget.unalignedFeedback: Looks can trick you — line the starting ends up first.
widget.missFeedback: Now the starts are lined up — check the far ends again: the one reaching farther is longer.
widget.successFeedback: The pole beats the string — half of the chain that will settle the pole against the rod.

predict.prompt: Two objects cannot be moved. Can a third object still settle which is longer?
predict.reveal: Each object is compared to the same go-between, and those two results settle the pair — provided the go-between falls between them; if both objects beat it, it is too short to decide, so use a longer one.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1m indirect.
invariants: The manipulated model and the measurement relationship for g1m indirect must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Reading a length from appearance or position instead of from same-size units laid end to end.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same measurement?

explanationVariants: Each object is compared to the same third thing.

widget.prompt: A pole is longer than a string (10 vs 6 units), and the string is longer than a rod (6 vs 5 units). What follows? Choose the key measurement idea.

options.label: The first is longer than the third
options.feedback: Correct — if the first beats the string and the string beats the third, the first must beat the third.

options.label: The third is longer than the first
options.feedback: That reverses the chain; each comparison points the same direction, so it cannot flip.

options.label: They are exactly equal
options.feedback: Both comparisons were strict, so the two objects cannot come out equal.

options.label: You must lay them side by side to know
options.feedback: A third object can settle it without moving either one — that is the point of indirect comparison.

hints: A third object can carry the comparison.

widget.prompt: Finish the chain: align the string and rod, then tap the longer one.
widget.unalignedFeedback: The string starts ahead. Align its start with the rod before using this link in the chain.
widget.missFeedback: Now the starts match. The farther end tells which link is longer.
widget.successFeedback: The string is longer than the rod, completing the second comparison in the chain.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Re-read the two lengths given, then compare them one step at a time.
